questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: The left position in the lane
The center position in the lane
The right position in the lane
There is no single best lane position for all situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position for all situations.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best, and no position should always be avoided. Choose a position that matches your riding conditions. This helps you stay safe and lets other drivers see you.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color helps drivers see you best?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Bright colors help other drivers see you. Bright red, orange, yellow, and green are best. Dark colors like black are harder for other drivers to see.

questions.question: What should you do if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Keep using the rear brake.
Swerve to the side with fewer hazards.
Try to accelerate while the brake is still engaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Release the brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. On a good surface, you can keep the brake locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When shifting into neutral
When you will slow down suddenly
When there is a stop sign ahead
When your signals are not working

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing suddenly. A driver tailgating you may be focused on your bike and not see hazards ahead that you are avoiding.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride below the speed limit
Rest your fingers on the clutch and brake levers
Shift into neutral when slowing
Speed up before turning

questions.correctAnswerText: Rest your fingers on the clutch and brake levers
questions.explanation: In dangerous areas like intersections, rest your fingers on the clutch and brake levers. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed
Avoid making sudden moves
Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, reduce speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these are more likely to be slippery.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear
Apply the rear brake first, then the front
Use both brakes at the same time
Use brakes in any order

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.

options.text: Farther away, more slowly
Farther away, faster
Closer, more slowly
Closer, faster

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Motorcycles look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge where you are and how fast you are going.

questions.question: If you must brake while turning, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road
Wait until you finish the curve to brake
Use only the rear brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road
questions.explanation: When leaning in a turn, tires have less grip. Try to straighten your bike before braking. If you must brake while turning, apply the brakes slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Six times
20 times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders with helmets, no matter how fast they are going.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the parking space so other drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb. Your rear wheel should touch the curb.

questions.question: What is true about rounded motorcycle mirrors?

options.text: They are easy to get used to right away.
They make cars seem closer than they really are.
They give you a narrow view of the road.
They make cars seem farther away than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make cars seem farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Rounded mirrors give you a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they actually are. Practice judging distances if you are not used to these mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Decrease the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road.
Wear tinted glasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road.
questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, slow down and increase your distance from other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles in front of you to see ahead. Change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal safely. But if you are in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: When stopping behind another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop far behind, then slowly creep up.
Stay well behind the vehicle.
Make a quick stop right behind it.
Stay about four car lengths behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when both are stopped. The vehicle could back up without warning. You also need space to escape if another vehicle comes toward you from behind.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. This is especially important in areas where hazards are likely.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride through a curve?

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a single-file formation.
In a side-by-side formation.
Using both lanes if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Ride in a single-file formation when going through curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway. Staggered formation is used in other situations.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning.
Lean in the direction you want to go when turning.
Avoid dragging your feet on the road.
Avoid looking at other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid looking at other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Do not drag your feet, as they could catch and cause you to lose control. Always watch for other traffic.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.
With your turn signal on.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center portion of your lane when being passed from behind. Riding closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: If you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action first, then the other.
Do both at the same time with extra braking pressure.
Do both at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.
Do not do either action.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. You need good grip on the road to swerve safely. Brake first, then swerve. Or swerve first, then brake.

questions.question: As an operator, what should you NOT tell a passenger to do before riding?

options.text: Get on after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Before riding, tell your passenger to get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you. They should hold onto the handholds or your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
Separate occasionally.
Ride in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: Riders should stay close together while leaving enough space around each rider to maneuver. Staying close makes the group easier to see and keeps riders from getting separated. Riding in pairs does not leave enough room to maneuver.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to be effective?

options.text: Fasten securely.
Prevent air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath.
Restrict your side vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: An eye or face shield must fasten securely. It should also be scratch-free, resist damage, allow clear side vision, let air pass through to stop fogging, and fit over eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use sudden pressure on the front brake to prevent the front tire from locking.
Only use the rear brake.
Use only one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the front brake lever gradually to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.
